chapters.title: Getting started with German

lessons.title: How this course works
lessons.summary: A short first meeting: what A1.1 covers, how a lesson runs, and what you should be able to do twelve chapters from now.
objectives: I know what the twelve chapters of A1.1 cover.
I know how a lesson is structured and what is expected of me.
I can say what I want to be able to do in German.

chapters.title: I can follow my first German lesson

lessons.title: Hello and goodbye
lessons.summary: The greetings that change with the clock, and the two ways to leave a room.
objectives: I can greet someone in German at any time of day.
I can say goodbye at the end of a class.
I can tell when to use du and when to use Sie.

lessons.title: Spelling my name out loud
lessons.summary: The German alphabet, and the handful of phrases that keep a lesson moving when you have not understood.
objectives: I can spell my name letter by letter.
I can ask someone to repeat something, or to speak more slowly.
I can ask what a word means and how it is written.

lessons.title: der, die, das
lessons.summary: Every German noun carries a gender. This lesson is about learning the article together with the word, from the first day.
objectives: I can name the three genders of German nouns.
I can use der, die and das with the nouns from this chapter.
I can write down a new noun the way it needs to be learned — with its article and its plural.

chapters.title: I can tell someone my name and where I'm from

lessons.title: Countries, cities and nationalities
lessons.summary: The country you come from, the city you live in, and the languages you speak.
objectives: I can name my country and my nationality in German.
I can say which languages I speak.
I can understand where someone else is from.

lessons.title: Introducing myself
lessons.summary: Four sentences that will introduce you for the rest of your life in German, and the questions that draw them out of someone else.
objectives: I can introduce myself with my name, my country and my city.
I can ask someone their name and where they come from.
I can introduce a third person.

lessons.title: Regular verbs in the present
lessons.summary: One stem, six endings. Once this pattern is in place, most German verbs follow it.
objectives: I can conjugate a regular verb in the present tense.
I can match the right ending to ich, du, er/sie, wir, ihr and sie/Sie.
I can build a simple sentence about myself with a regular verb.

chapters.title: I can give my phone number, my address and my age

lessons.title: Numbers from zero to a hundred
lessons.summary: Counting, and the trick that makes German numbers hard to hear: the units are said before the tens.
objectives: I can count from zero to a hundred.
I can understand a number said out loud at normal speed.
I can say my age and my year of birth.

lessons.title: Filling in a form
lessons.summary: Surname, first name, date of birth, postcode. The fields that appear on every German form, and how to dictate them over a counter.
objectives: I can give my address, my postcode and my phone number.
I can understand the labels on a simple German form.
I can ask someone to repeat a number.

lessons.title: sein and haben
lessons.summary: The two verbs that refuse to follow the pattern, and the two you need most.
objectives: I can conjugate sein and haben in the present tense.
I can say how old I am and what I have.
I can tell the difference between where sein is used and where haben is.

chapters.title: I can buy food and pay for it

lessons.title: Food, drink, and the shops that sell them
lessons.summary: What is sold at the bakery, the butcher and the supermarket, and the words for weights and packets.
objectives: I can name the everyday foods I buy each week.
I can say which shop sells what.
I can use the German words for a kilo, a pound and a packet.

lessons.title: At the till
lessons.summary: Asking for a quantity, hearing a price, and paying without slowing the queue down.
objectives: I can ask for an amount of something.
I can ask what something costs and understand the answer.
I can say whether I am paying in cash or by card.

lessons.title: The accusative
lessons.summary: When a noun is the thing being bought, eaten or taken, der becomes den. This is the first case change in the course.
objectives: I can explain what the accusative marks in a sentence.
I can use den, die, das and einen, eine, ein after verbs like kaufen and nehmen.
I can spot the one article that actually changes.

chapters.title: I can order in a café and read a menu

lessons.title: On the menu
lessons.summary: Breakfast, cake and the drinks list — enough of a Speisekarte to order from without pointing.
objectives: I can read a simple German menu.
I can name what I usually eat and drink.
I can say what I do not eat.

lessons.title: Ordering and paying at a table
lessons.summary: Being seated, ordering, asking for the bill, and the small politeness that goes with each.
objectives: I can order food and drink at a table.
I can ask for the bill and say whether we are paying together or separately.
I can understand what a waiter asks me.

lessons.title: Asking questions
lessons.summary: Two shapes: the ones that start with a question word, and the ones that start with the verb.
objectives: I can ask a yes/no question by putting the verb first.
I can use wer, was, wo, wann, wie and wie viel.
I can tell which of the two question shapes a sentence is using.

chapters.title: I can tell someone what time it is

lessons.title: The 24-hour clock
lessons.summary: How Germany writes and says times officially — timetables, opening hours, appointments.
objectives: I can read a time written as 14:30 and say it aloud.
I can name the parts of the day.
I can understand opening hours on a sign.

lessons.title: Asking and telling the time
lessons.summary: The everyday spoken clock, where halb drei means half past two and catches everyone out once.
objectives: I can ask what time it is.
I can say a time using Viertel, halb and vor/nach.
I can say when something opens, starts or closes.

lessons.title: Saying when: um, am, von … bis
lessons.summary: Small words that decide whether you are talking about a clock time, a day, or a stretch of time.
objectives: I can use um for clock times and am for days.
I can give a span of time with von … bis.
I can put a time expression in the right place in a sentence.

chapters.title: I can name the day, the date and the month

lessons.title: Days, months and seasons
lessons.summary: The seven days, the twelve months, the four seasons, and the words for yesterday, today and tomorrow.
objectives: I can name the days of the week and the months of the year.
I can name the four seasons.
I can say when something happens using heute, morgen and am Wochenende.

lessons.title: Making an appointment
lessons.summary: Suggesting a time, accepting, refusing politely and moving it — by phone and in person.
objectives: I can suggest a day and a time for a meeting.
I can accept or turn down a suggested time.
I can ask to move an appointment.

lessons.title: Dates and ordinal numbers
lessons.summary: Why the first of May is der erste Mai, and how a German date changes shape depending on where it sits.
objectives: I can form ordinal numbers from one to thirty-one.
I can say and write a full date.
I can say the date of my birthday.

chapters.title: I can describe an ordinary day

lessons.title: Verbs that come apart
lessons.summary: aufstehen, anfangen, einkaufen — the daily-routine verbs whose prefix jumps to the end of the sentence.
objectives: I can name the everyday actions that fill a normal day.
I can recognise a separable verb from its prefix.
I can send the prefix to the end of the sentence where it belongs.

lessons.title: Telling someone about my day
lessons.summary: Stringing the day together in order, from waking up to going to bed, and asking someone about theirs.
objectives: I can describe my day in the order it happens.
I can say how often I do something.
I can ask someone what their day looks like.

lessons.title: The verb comes second
lessons.summary: German will move almost anything to the front of a sentence — as long as the verb stays in position two.
objectives: I can keep the conjugated verb in second position.
I can start a sentence with a time expression without breaking it.
I can order time, manner and place in a sentence.

chapters.title: I can get across town by bus, tram and train

lessons.title: Buses, trams, trains and tickets
lessons.summary: The vehicles, the stops, the platforms and the machine that sells you the ticket.
objectives: I can name the kinds of public transport in a German city.
I can understand the words on a ticket machine.
I can name the parts of a station.

lessons.title: At the station
lessons.summary: Buying the right ticket, finding the platform, and understanding an announcement well enough not to miss the train.
objectives: I can buy a ticket for a particular journey.
I can ask which platform a train leaves from.
I can ask whether this is the right bus or tram.

lessons.title: Prepositions that take the dative
lessons.summary: mit, zu, von, nach, aus, bei — after these, der becomes dem and die becomes der.
objectives: I can list the prepositions that are always followed by the dative.
I can use dem, der and den with those prepositions.
I can say how I travel and where I am going.

chapters.title: I can say what I do for a living

lessons.title: Jobs and workplaces
lessons.summary: Job titles and the places they are done in — and the fact that German makes a separate word for a woman doing the job.
objectives: I can name common jobs in German.
I can form the female version of a job title.
I can say where I work.

lessons.title: Talking about my working day
lessons.summary: What you do, who you do it with, and the hours — the answer to the question every new acquaintance asks.
objectives: I can say what my job is and what it involves.
I can say what hours and days I work.
I can ask someone else about their job.

lessons.title: Verbs that change their vowel
lessons.summary: sprechen becomes du sprichst, fahren becomes du fährst. A small group of very common verbs shifts its vowel for du and er/sie.
objectives: I can recognise the verbs that change their stem vowel.
I can conjugate them correctly for du and er/sie.
I can use them to talk about myself and one other person.

chapters.title: I can say what I like doing and what I don't

lessons.title: Hobbies, sport and screens
lessons.summary: What people actually do with an evening or a Sunday, from football to television.
objectives: I can name my hobbies in German.
I can name common sports and say which I play.
I can say what I do at the weekend.

lessons.title: Saying what I like, and suggesting something
lessons.summary: gern, lieber and am liebsten — and how to turn a preference into an invitation.
objectives: I can say what I like doing using gern.
I can say what I prefer.
I can suggest doing something together and respond to a suggestion.

lessons.title: Saying no: nicht and kein
lessons.summary: German has two negatives and they are not interchangeable. One negates a noun, the other everything else.
objectives: I can choose between nicht and kein.
I can put nicht in the right place in a sentence.
I can say what I do not do and do not have.

chapters.title: I can handle the post office, the bank and a form

lessons.title: The counter, the form and the queue
lessons.summary: The words that appear on German official paperwork — Antrag, Formular, Schalter, Termin — and the places that hand it to you.
objectives: I can name the services at a post office and a bank.
I can understand the common words on an official form.
I can name the documents I am usually asked for.

lessons.title: Asking for what I need at a counter
lessons.summary: Stating your business in one sentence, asking for help with a form, and making an appointment at an office.
objectives: I can say what I have come to do.
I can ask for help filling in a form.
I can make an appointment at an office.

lessons.title: können, müssen, dürfen
lessons.summary: The verbs for can, must and may — they take a second verb and send it, unchanged, to the end of the sentence.
objectives: I can conjugate können, müssen and dürfen.
I can put the second verb at the end in its infinitive form.
I can say what I can, must and am allowed to do.

chapters.title: Where I stand at the end of A1.1

lessons.title: Level check
lessons.summary: A conversation across all twelve chapters, ending with a short written record of what is solid and what to take into A1.2.
objectives: I can hold a short conversation drawing on all twelve chapters.
I can see which chapters I still need to practise.
I know what A1.2 will ask of me.
